distinguishing_features: Uses a sacrificial Mg-Zr or Zn-In anode array rather than chemical dosing or monitoring
Directly couples the sacrificial array electrically to the titanium anode bus
Uses anolyte conductivity and close electrode spacing to limit ohmic potential loss
Defines an electrochemical potential criterion and polarization-test kill condition for protection
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to suppress chloride-induced corrosion and pitting of a titanium anode coating while sustaining industrial anodic current density in highly conductive chlor-alkali anolyte.
parsed.viable_reason: The titanium electrode is held at an anodic potential by the cell power supply, so the directly connected sacrificial rods cannot cathodically protect it and would instead be driven to anodic dissolution in the same electrolyte.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Although the hardware arrangement is distinctive, sacrificial-anode cathodic protection is a routine corrosion-control concept and is not a viable departure for a deliberately anodic titanium electrode.
